newsitem.title: USA: NY jury finds 10 violated access law to clinic.
newsitem.headline: NY jury finds 10 violated access law to clinic.

text.p: Ten people who were charged with blocking the entrance to a New York City abortion clinic last summer under a 1994 federal access law were found liable by a civil jury on Thursday.

"Today's verdict puts those who would deliberately interfere with the constitutional right of reproductive choice on notice that this conduct will not be tolerated," Mary Jo White, the U.S. attorney, said in a statement after the verdict.
She also said the government would seek an injunction that would bar the defendants from blocking access to any abortion clinic in the nation.
U.S. District Judge John Sprizzo, who presided over the three day trial, will determine the damages in a second proceeding that may include a jury.

According to the civil complaint filed on July 23, 1996, the group of mostly male defendants pushed their way past a security guard at the Eastern Women's Centre in midtown Manhattan and occupied the clinic's main waiting room.
The clinic offers reproductive health services.
During the trial, the government proved that five of the defendants chained themselves together using bicycle locks and blocked the door to doctors' offices and testing facilities.
Other defendants lay in front of the elevators, blocking incoming patients, and sat in front of other clinic doors.
As a result of the blockade, the clinic was unable to operate for nearly three hours until police could cut the locks.
